title: Orchestrate daemon starts from one typed configuration object
description: The Datom path-lock epic proves the stripped registry, but orchestrate-daemon still accepts four raw positional filesystem paths for store and sockets. This predates the epic and conflicts with the Nexus startup contract. See epic branch epic-datom-path-locks-20260822 and the independent audit of orchestrate-fv7.
design: In a separate bite, replace raw startup paths with one typed signal-encoded configuration object, update daemon construction and isolated scenario wiring, and keep production migration out of the path-lock epic.
acceptance_criteria: Daemon accepts exactly one typed configuration input; raw multi-positional startup is absent; sandbox uses the typed configuration with temporary store/socket values; failing-first tests and the durable Nix gate pass.

title: Path locks register through Datom
description: Current lane registration is over-specified and Dotos-bound. Inspect the isolated epic workspaces in Datom, Signal Orchestrate, Meta Signal Orchestrate, and Orchestrate, together with flow 01a02a34, before implementation. The work must replace that boundary with an ordinary path-lock registration and keep all test execution isolated from production state.
design: Use a native Datom carrier and ordinary Signal registration of {name, paths, description}. Normalize registered paths and reject any overlap all-or-nothing. Prove registration through isolated sockets and stores; do not mutate the filesystem. Omit Ethos unless its readiness is directly witnessed.
acceptance_criteria: Four matching pushed epic branches exist. Datom has a round-trip witness. Signal has a frame round-trip witness. An isolated service witnesses registration, normalized overlap conflict, persistence, and no filesystem mutation. Durable Nix gates cover the behavior.
notes:
Epic branches and isolated workspaces are pushed across datom, signal-orchestrate, meta-signal-orchestrate, and orchestrate. Datom native path-lock carrier implementation is in progress; Ethos generation was witnessed not ready, so no legacy Schema or false Ethos artifact will be added.
Datom 0.2.0 native PathLock carrier landed on epic-datom-path-locks-20260822 at 1b60b0c864ab. Canonical text: PathLock.{datom [/home/li/primary /var/lock] (protect the active paths)}. Datom failing-first test and full Nix gate passed. Ordinary Signal contract implementation is in progress.
signal-orchestrate 0.14.0 landed at 52c43ed0ed165a04fe0d77a4a9ee103c903f9d5c. Ordinary wire is Register(PathLock) with PathLockRegistered or typed DuplicateActiveName/PathOverlap rejection; Datom conversion is native; Dotos/legacy lane aggregate removed; full Nix gate green. Meta signal alignment is next.
meta-signal-orchestrate 0.9.0/wire 2 landed at e92e4667cbfb. It pins signal 0.14.0 and retains only self-contained RefreshRepositoryIndex; obsolete lane/session/role/authority/recovery/worktree-registry and Dotos surfaces removed. Full Nix gate green. Orchestrate implementation is in progress.
Datom carrier validation corrected at ac5198235cdf: private three-field PathLock, checked constructor, name/description/path invariants, failing-first constructor and compile-fail witnesses, full Nix gate green. Native Datom registered/rejected reply carriers are now in progress so CLI replies remain typed instead of falling back to stderr.
Final dependency line: datom 0.2.0 at 4435f763af57 with validated PathLock plus native registered/rejected carriers; signal-orchestrate 0.15.0/wire3 at a038c5c04fea5ff4a5ffcecfd0c9cdcc284d611f with lossless reply conversions; meta-signal-orchestrate 0.9.0/wire2 at f1dec7e3f7b0 pinning final Signal and retaining only RefreshRepositoryIndex. All dependency Nix gates green. Orchestrate final integration is in progress.
Independent audit: all four epic workspaces clean/pushed with a single Datom 4435 -> Signal a038 -> Meta f1dec / Orchestrate de59 chain. Full Nix gates pass in all four. Orchestrate stateful sandbox passed fresh plus 25 consecutive runs with temp store/sockets, inotify event waits, restart duplicate-name witness, and filesystem non-mutation assertions. Existing raw four-path daemon startup was separated as discovered follow-up orchestrate-yjo. Low nonruntime stale coordination.ethos/bootstrap text remains on the Signal epic and is not compiled or consumed.
close_reason: Implemented on pushed epic-datom-path-locks-20260822 branches: Datom 4435f763 (native validated lock and typed replies), Signal a038c5c0 (0.15.0/wire3 Register contract), Meta f1dec7e3 (0.9.0/wire2 stripped refresh-only contract), Orchestrate de59c3f7 (0.21.0 durable registry and Datom CLI). Failing-first tests were observed. Full Nix gates pass in all four repositories. The isolated daemon scenario uses temporary store/socket paths, event waits, persists across restart, preserves existing files, leaves absent paths absent, and passed 25 consecutive independent audit runs. Raw daemon startup is separate follow-up orchestrate-yjo.
